scenes.line1: Can you subnet in your head?
scenes.line2: How many hosts in a slash 26?
scenes.say: Can you quickly tell how many hosts fit in a slash twenty-six subnet? Let's make subnetting second nature.

scenes.label: Network Bits
scenes.sub: Fewer network bits means more hosts per subnet.
scenes.say: The slash number is how many bits make up the network part. Fewer network bits means more room for hosts.
Here's a cheat sheet. Slash twenty-four gives you two hundred fifty-four usable addresses. Each step up halves the number. Slash twenty-six? Sixty-two usable hosts.
Remember these private address ranges. Ten dot zero, one seventy-two dot sixteen, and one ninety-two dot one sixty-eight. They're for internal networks only.

scenes.question: How many usable hosts in /28?
scenes.right: 14 usable hosts. Two addresses are reserved.
scenes.say: Watch out! In a slash twenty-eight, you get fourteen usable hosts, not sixteen. Two addresses are always reserved for network and broadcast.
